newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Peru fails to reach agreement with Andean Pact.
newsitem.headline: Peru fails to reach agreement with Andean Pact.

text.p: Efforts toward regional economic integration suffered another setback after Peru failed to reach agreement with Andean Pact countries to fully rejoin the free trade group it broke with in 1992, Colombian Foreign Trade Minister Carlos Ronderos said.
"Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela and Bolivia found Peru's proposal for joining the free trade zone unacceptable," he told reporters late Thursday.

He and his Andean Pact colleagues met over 12 hours with Gustavo Caillaux, Peru's minister of Industry, Tourism and Integration, to discuss Lima's proposal for a gradual lifting of trade and tariff barriers that would put it on an equal footing with other Andean Pact countries within seven years.
Ronderos stressed that there was no immediate decision to expel Peru from the Andean Pact or impose commercial sanctions against it.
But he said the presidents of member countries would have the final word on what if any action should be taken.
The Andean Pact presidents are to hold a two-day summit in Sucre, Bolivia, later this month.

Peru cited incompatibilities between its foreign trade policy and the Andean Pact's system of commun trade tariffs when it pulled out of the free trade bloc amid a deep economic crisis in 1992. Caillaux stressed that it would remain an active member of the Lima-based group at a political level, however.
